Refuted by measurement — reverted, no code change.

Micro-benchmark (60 wipes, 3 alternating rounds, tests/helpers/db against the real *_test DB):
  A 26 sequential deleteMany (current) :   4.9ms/wipe
  B one TRUNCATE ... CASCADE           : 146.3ms/wipe  (~30x SLOWER)
  C $transaction([...deleteMany]) batch:   5.5ms/wipe  (no better than A)

Full-suite confirmation: TRUNCATE runs measured 110.7s and 143.6s vs a 45-60s baseline (3 runs) - consistent with ~400 wipes x 146ms.

Root of the error: the premise 'the cost is 26 round trips of latency' is false. Against localhost with empty fixture tables, 26 deleteMany round trips total ~5ms. TRUNCATE pays per-table file truncation + fsync, which dominates completely at this data size. wipeAll() is NOT a bottleneck and is not worth optimizing.

Implication for autoknow-zks: the 5s->20s testTimeout bump (autoknow-gj0) cannot have been caused by round-trip COUNT, since the nominal wipe is ~5ms. It points at contention on the ONE shared test database - which is what per-worker DB isolation addresses.
